mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when inflation exceeds 4%.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism does not activate during a confirmed NBER recession.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 8% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered months, or the mechanism fails during periods of strong wage growth.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% for three consecutive months indicates weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate earnings and capital expenditure, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism does not activate when supply shocks are exogenous.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in the federal funds rate and a decline in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 0.5% in the same month signals a restrictive monetary policy coinciding with falling inflation, which typically precedes equity market corrections over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises AND CPIAUCSL falls > 0.5% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.7%) in at least 50% of triggered months, or the mechanism fails when GDP growth exceeds 3%.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average by more than 10% for two consecutive months signals a housing market recovery, which boosts construction-related equities and supports broader market gains over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during periods of rising mortgage rates.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both payroll employment (PAYEMS) and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) in the same month indicates a statistical artifact of labor force reclassification rather than genuine job creation, which historically precedes equity market volatility and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS rises AND UNRATE rises in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.3%) in at least 55% of triggered months, or the mechanism does not activate outside of major census months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) above its 12-month moving average by more than 15% for four consecutive months signals elevated precautionary savings, which typically coincides with reduced consumer spending and negative corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.6%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during periods of rising household debt.
